operating_notes.text: Total bed capacity increased to 6,464 beds across various regional clusters in FY26.
New units contributed ₹224 Cr to Q4 revenue with an EBITDA erosion of ₹32 Cr.
IP volumes 72,493 (+26.6% YoY), OP volumes 6,58,617 (+28.5% YoY).
Thane July revenue ₹21 Cr vs Q1 average ₹16 Cr, 10% EBITDA margin.
Mahadevapura July revenue ₹20 Cr, near breakeven; Electronic City expected breakeven by year-end.
Target company Sarvottam Health Care Private Limited operates 183-bed Trust Multi Speciality Hospital in Kakinada with FY26 turnover of ₹84.83 Cr and PAT of ₹7.06 Cr.
Target Ushahkal Abhinav Specialty Hospital LLP operates a 316-bed facility in Sangli with FY26 turnover of ₹80.42 Cr, PAT of ₹-23.59 Cr, and net worth of ₹116.42 Cr.
KIMS Saveera Hospital, Anantapur expanded from 250 to 500 beds, adding an oncology block (HD-LINAC, Digital PET-CT, Brachytherapy) and a mother-and-child block with NICU.

timeline.summary: KIMS signed a non-commercial clinical collaboration MoU with Dakshayani Healthcare Services (Renova) for oncology services.
KIMS signed a 60-year lease agreement with APCRDA for 2 acres of land in Amaravati to build a 500-bed multi-speciality hospital.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹1,074.6 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹42.5 Cr (-58.3% YoY).
KIMS released its FY26 investor presentation detailing operational performance, revenue of ₹3,904.6 Cr, and bed capacity expansion to 6,464 beds.
KIMS reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,084 Cr and PAT of ₹33 Cr, impacted by expansion costs, and announced plans for a ₹1,500 Cr QIP.
Q1FY27 earnings call: revenue ₹1,196 Cr (+36.1% YoY), PAT ₹37 Cr; QIP raised ₹1,500 Cr, debt cut to ₹2,570 Cr.
KIMS entered into definitive agreements to acquire a 51% stake in Sarvottam Health Care Private Limited (183 beds in Kakinada) for up to ₹79.50 Cr.
KIMS executed definitive agreements and invested ₹15 Cr for a 5.82% stake in Ushahkal Abhinav Specialty Hospital LLP (316 beds in Sangli).

2026-11-01: KIMS Saveera Hospital, Anantapur (Saveera Institute of Medical Sciences subsidiary) expanded from 250 to 500 beds, adding an oncology block with HD-LINAC and PET-CT and a mother-and-child block.
